# FDG9057

> DO NOT put code in the property accessors other than the standard code to access the static field.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 9.3.1 Dependency Property Design.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG9057
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: draft

Message: Remove the code other than the {1} call from the accessor of the dependency property '{0}'

FDG9057 reports an accessor of the CLR property of a dependency property, which is a property P of a class derived from DependencyObject that declares a static DependencyProperty field named P followed by "Property" that calls GetValue or SetValue with the field (as FDG9054 checks) and holds other code too: the standard get accessor only returns the result of GetValue, cast or converted to the property type, and the standard set accessor only calls SetValue with the field and the value parameter. Validation, change notification and coercion in accessors (FDG9059, FDG9060, FDG9061) are such code, and FDG9057 reports them. Wrappers that FDG9054 does not find are not seen, so coverage is partial. The fix moves the code into the callbacks of the registration; there is no code fix.

## From the book

That code won’t execute if the property is set by implicit means, such as a styling, because styling uses the static field directly.

```csharp
public string Text {
  get { return (string)GetValue(TextProperty); }
  set {
    SetValue(TextProperty, value);
    DoWorkOnTextChanged(); // this is bad!
  }
}
```
